1.1.title: The rule and the two kinds of job
1.1.say: The rule: every document the Command writes does one job. A page that tries to do two becomes two pages.

1.2.title: The four types
1.2.say: Tutorial: a lesson; the reader learns by doing it start to finish.

2.1.title: Name three things first
2.1.say: Who it's for: the reader, and the situation they open it in ("Chief, mid-session" · "a new writer on OXO").

2.2.title: Owner, state, reviewed date
2.2.say: Owner: who decides what the page says.

2.3.title: Where the header sits
2.3.say: The 2.1 three show up top, in the one thin strip at the head of the page: who it's for · what it does · which type.

3.1.title: One term per thing
3.1.say: One word for each thing, and only that word. If it's the "register," it is never also "the list" or "the catalog."

3.2.title: Short sentences, someone doing something
3.2.say: One idea per sentence. A sentence that needs "and" twice splits.

3.4.title: Review in passes
3.4.say: Separate reads, one job each: (1) facts: true and current? (2) words: one term per thing (3.1), short sentences (3.2)? (3) out loud: does it read clean spoken?

4.1.title: The troubleshooting page
4.1.say: Start from what the reader sees: the error or the problem, not how the system works.

4.2.title: The glossary page
4.2.say: One entry per term, in alphabetical order.

4.3.title: The decision record
4.3.say: One decision per page, dated, with who ruled it.
